overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance indicates massive audience demand for extreme planetary 'What-If' scenarios and bizarre space oddities with high sensory contrast (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?'). Videos focused on hypothetical extreme space survival, unusual planetary physics, and visceral curiosity hooks generated significantly higher views-per-day and like-to-view ratios compared to standard abstract science or older static trivia.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views in ~5 days) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) vastly outperform standard static fact statements.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical immersion formats where the viewer interacts with extreme cosmic environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,026 views) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) show exceptional organic pull within the space and astronomy niche.
winning_patterns.action: Prioritize celestial bodies featuring paradoxical elements like extreme temperatures, strange precipitation, or unusual light absorption.

weak_patterns.pattern: Abstract Psychological & Biological Trivia without Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) generated negligible traction during recent tracking windows.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize flat psychological trivia unless framed through an urgent, high-stakes personal survival or visceral micro-story hook.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve' plateaued early at 139 views, indicating weaker initial hook retention compared to spatial extremes.
weak_patterns.action: Refine historical storytelling hooks to feature more immediate sensory danger or bizarre unexplained physical anomalies.
